Subject: SLA incident: closure notes + owners (action grid for QBR)

Team / Elaine,

Attached is a concise draft of the postmortem for the August 21st SLA incident (impact window ~11:04–11:43 PDT). This draft is intended for QBR prep and executive summary distribution; please review the owners and committed dates in the action grid section. High-level summary below — full timeline and evidence in the attached CSV.

Impact summary:
- What: Token-serving pipeline saturated on a small subset of bursts, resulting in elevated 95th/99th latency and ~6.5% error spike for hosted API customers.
- Who: ~1.2k requests impacted (Acme Retail accounts most visible due to long-context workloads).
- When: Aug 21, 11:04–11:43 PDT.
- Severity: SLA threshold breached for two minutes (post-rollout circuit breaker misclassification).

Root cause (current working hypothesis):
- A recent kernel change increased tail latency for long-sequence decoders under specific batching patterns. This interacted with request-level routing that favored a single GPU pool during a regional burst, amplifying queuing.

Immediate mitigations completed (Aug 21–22):
1) Routing fallback toggled to conservative policy (Hannah) — instantaneous containment.
2) Hotfix reverted kernel selector to previous version for the affected pool (Jonas) — validated in staging and rolled to prod.
3) Temporary throughput cap applied for long-context routes while we assess batching knobs (Marissa).

Open commitments (action grid) — please confirm owner/date for QBR packet: 
- A1: Full kernel compatibility test matrix + automated regression (owner: Hannah, due: 2026-09-10)
- A2: Durable routing policy with chaos test (owner: Jonas, due: 2026-09-03)
- A3: Workload-aware batching defaults + opt-in per-customer profile (owner: Marissa, due: 2026-09-17)
- A4: SLA measurement post-change (owner: Vivek, due: 2026-09-08)

For leadership: I expect the above will close the most material failure modes. For the QBR summary I propose a single-slide exec narrative: 1) What happened 2) Containment 3) Commitments & dates.

Please reply with any edits to owners/dates. Elaine — curious if the remediation plan and the temporary credit offer are acceptable from Acme Retail side; tagging you for confirmation.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-ACME-20260828.docx, slo-incident-timeline-ACME.csv

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Director, Incident & Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick technical updates to include in the postmortem: 
- Kernel selector change that triggered the issue: the selector prioritized an "aggressive" quantization kernel for >2k token sequences when CPU offload was enabled. That kernel has a known transient GC behavior at high batch sizes which we missed in canary because the input distribution was short-context.
- Test plan I propose: a compatibility matrix that runs the long-context QA harness at three batch-size distributions (1x, 4x, 12x) across all kernels during nightly regression; results posted to INF-3472 (Jira).
- I'll attach the ops runbook patch (ops-runbook-patch-20260829.pdf) which documents rollback steps and the gating for automatic fallback.

Action notes: A1 updated owner/date confirmed: Hannah — 2026-09-10. I will create the GHA workflow and link it in the drive doc by Monday 8/31.

Hannah
Director, Serving Runtime

Chloe / team — following up on A3 (batching defaults). Quick status and ask: 

- We scoped two paths: conservative defaults (fast to ship, higher per-token cost) vs. perf-optimized profile (longer runway, lower cost). Recommend shipping conservative defaults as a short-term safety net and the profile opt-in for customers in the next sprint.
- Provisional dates: conservative defaults -> 2026-09-03; perf-profile opt-in -> 2026-09-17. I can move conservative to 9/02 if that helps QBR narrative.
- Cost delta estimate for the conservative defaults: +3.2% token cost on affected long-context customers (rough estimate; will finalize with billing).

I will add the 1-line cost summary into the postmortem doc and update the action grid.

Marissa
